fields.title: Autoimmune thyroiditis
fields.bodyHtml:
Autoimmune thyroiditis: advanced treatment in Israel

Autoimmune thyroiditis, also known as chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis or Hashimoto's disease, is the most common autoimmune condition of the thyroid gland. In this condition the immune system mistakenly attacks the tissue of the thyroid, which can lead to hypothyroidism — an underactive thyroid. Israel takes a comprehensive approach to diagnosing and treating autoimmune thyroiditis, drawing on the latest research and innovative techniques.

Diagnosis of autoimmune thyroiditis:

  1. Blood tests for thyroid hormones
    Levels of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) and of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) are measured to assess thyroid function. Antibodies to thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) and thyroglobulin are identified, which helps confirm the autoimmune nature of the condition.
  2. Ultrasound examination of the thyroid gland
    Allows the structure and size of the gland and the presence of nodules to be assessed.
  3. Fine needle biopsy (where necessary)
    Used to rule out cancer of the thyroid if suspicious nodules are found.

Treatment of autoimmune thyroiditis in Israel:

  1. Hormone replacement therapy
    with levothyroxine to make up the deficit of thyroid hormones.
  2. Individual adjustment of drug doses
    based on regular monitoring of the TSH level.
  3. Thyroidectomy
    Surgical removal of the thyroid gland or part of it may be recommended where drug treatment is ineffective, where the gland is considerably enlarged and presses on neighbouring structures, or where suspicious nodules are present. In Israel, thyroid operations are often performed using minimally invasive techniques, including laparoscopic methods.
  4. Treatment with iodine-containing preparations
    where there is iodine deficiency.
  5. Comprehensive support
    Consultations with a dietitian and psychological support to improve general health and help manage stress.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israeli doctors have considerable experience in diagnosing and treating autoimmune thyroid disease.
  • Advanced medical technology
    The use of modern equipment and techniques ensures accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach
    Attention to every patient and account taken of their particular circumstances and preferences when the treatment plan is drawn up.
  • Close collaboration between specialists
    Endocrinologists, surgeons, dietitians and psychologists work closely together to provide comprehensive care.

Treatment of autoimmune thyroiditis in Israel is aimed at controlling symptoms, normalising thyroid function and preventing complications, which allows patients to lead an active and healthy life.

fields.title: Azoospermia
fields.bodyHtml:
Azoospermia: advanced treatment in Israel

Azoospermia is the absence of sperm in the ejaculate and is one of the causes of male infertility. In Israel, modern methods are used to diagnose and treat azoospermia, giving many men hope of fatherhood.

Diagnosis of azoospermia:

  1. Repeat semen analysis
    Several semen analyses are recommended to confirm the diagnosis, since results can vary.
  2. Laboratory tests
    Blood tests for the hormones that regulate the work of the reproductive glands (testosterone, FSH, LH, prolactin) help establish the type of azoospermia (obstructive or non-obstructive).
  3. Genetic tests
    Carried out to identify chromosomal abnormalities or specific genetic mutations that may be the cause of azoospermia.
  4. Transrectal ultrasound
    Used to assess the state of the sperm ducts and detect possible obstruction.
  5. Testicular biopsy
    Carried out to obtain testicular tissue for examination under the microscope and to look for sperm.

The plan of investigation is drawn up individually and can take up to two days, after which the results are awaited and a detailed consultation with the doctor follows. For more information, contact our free adviser (we will review medical records from your own country if you have them).

Methods of treating azoospermia in Israel:

  1. Surgical treatment of obstructive azoospermia
    Includes operations to restore the patency of the sperm ducts, such as vasovasostomy or vasoepididymostomy.
  2. Treatment of non-obstructive azoospermia
    Aimed at stimulating sperm production with hormone therapy, where the cause of the condition allows.
  3. Assisted reproductive technologies
    Where sperm are found in the testis or epididymis, they can be used for fertilisation within IVF/ICSI programmes. Methods of retrieving sperm include TESE (testicular sperm extraction), TESA (testicular sperm aspiration) and others.
  4. Advice on the use of donor sperm
    Where sperm cannot be obtained, couples may consider using donor sperm to conceive.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A personalised approach: an individual treatment plan for every patient, depending on the cause of the azoospermia.
  • A multidisciplinary team: urologists, endocrinologists, geneticists and fertility specialists take part in treatment, ensuring a comprehensive approach.
  • Use of modern technology: Israel's leading clinics are equipped with the latest diagnostic and treatment equipment, which improves the chances of success.
  • A high level of expertise: Israeli specialists have international recognition in the treatment of male infertility and in introducing innovative techniques.

Treatment of azoospermia in Israel offers men advanced solutions aimed at making fatherhood possible despite difficult diagnoses, with comprehensive support at every stage of treatment.

fields.title: Barrett's oesophagus
fields.bodyHtml:
Barrett's oesophagus: advanced treatment in Israel

Barrett's oesophagus is a condition in which the normal cells lining the lower part of the oesophagus are replaced by cells not typical of that area. This can increase the risk of developing adenocarcinoma of the oesophagus. Modern methods of diagnosis and treatment are used in Israel to monitor the condition and prevent it progressing.

Diagnosis of Barrett's oesophagus:

  1. Endoscopy with biopsy
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the altered areas of the lining to be seen and tissue samples taken for histological analysis.
  2. Biopsy with radiofrequency ablation
    Used to remove or reduce the volume of abnormal tissue.
  3. Immunocytochemical studies
    Identification of molecular markers that may indicate an increased risk of progression to cancer.
  4. Chromoendoscopy
    The use of special dyes during endoscopy for better visualisation of abnormal cells.

Methods of treating Barrett's oesophagus:

  1. Radiofrequency ablation (RFA):
    • A minimally invasive procedure that uses radiofrequency waves to destroy the altered cells without damaging the surrounding tissue.
  2. Endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR):
    • Removal of abnormal areas of the lining of the oesophagus using specialised endoscopic equipment.
  3. Drug treatment:
    • Proton pump inhibitors to reduce the acidity of the stomach contents, which helps lessen irritation of the lining of the oesophagus and supports healing.
  4. Diet and lifestyle changes:
    • Changes in eating habits, including avoiding late meals and reducing the intake of fatty and spicy food and alcohol.
    • Maintaining a healthy weight and avoiding tight clothing.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A personalised approach to every patient: treatment based on individual characteristics and the stage of the condition.
  • Use of advanced technology: the introduction of the newest methods of diagnosis and treatment, which improves the chances of a good outcome.
  • Multidisciplinary medical teams: experienced gastroenterologists, surgeons and oncologists work together to ensure a comprehensive approach to treatment.
  • A high standard of medical care: excellent quality of medical services and attention to detail in patient care.
  • Education and rehabilitation: patients are given all the information they need about the condition and its treatment, along with advice on lifestyle changes to minimise the risk of recurrence.

Treatment of Barrett's oesophagus in Israel is aimed at minimising the risk of oesophageal cancer and improving patients' quality of life through accurate diagnosis, effective treatment and continuing medical follow-up.

fields.title: Basal cell carcinoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Basal cell carcinoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Basal cell carcinoma is the most common type of skin cancer. It grows slowly and rarely spreads, but without proper treatment it can cause considerable damage to the skin and the tissues beneath it. In Israel, patients with basal cell carcinoma are offered a wide range of modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, aimed at preserving as much healthy skin as possible and preventing recurrence.

Diagnosis of basal cell carcinoma

  1. Dermoscopy
    Detailed examination of suspicious areas of skin using a special magnifying device that allows the structure of the lesion to be assessed.
  2. Laboratory tests
    May be carried out to assess the patient's general health and identify associated conditions.
  3. Consultation with a dermatological surgeon
    This stage is critically important for planning further treatment.

Treatment of basal cell carcinoma

  1. Mohs micrographic surgery
    A highly effective technique for treating basal cell carcinoma that removes as little healthy tissue as possible and reduces the risk of recurrence.
  2. Cryotherapy
    The use of liquid nitrogen to freeze and destroy tumour cells, used for small basal cell carcinomas.
  3. Laser therapy
    May be used to remove superficial tumours without damaging the surrounding tissue.
  4. Photodynamic therapy
    A combination of light and photosensitising agents to destroy cancer cells.
  5. Topical immunotherapy
    The use of creams or ointments containing anti-cancer or immune-modulating agents to treat superficial basal cell carcinomas.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists: Israeli dermatologists and oncologists have rich experience in diagnosing and treating every type of skin cancer, basal cell carcinoma included.
  • Modern equipment: Israeli medical institutions are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment technology.
  • An individual approach: every patient is offered the treatment that best suits their needs, taking account of the stage of the disease and their general health.
  • Integrated support: patients receive full support at every stage of treatment, from diagnosis through to recovery.

Treatment of basal cell carcinoma in Israel gives patients access to effective and safe therapies, aimed not only at removing the tumour but at preserving quality of life as fully as possible.
